en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Goddess Mārīcī, translated by an unknown person and now appended to the Liang Records.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada.
At the Jeta Grove,
together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
the World-Honored One then addressed the bhikṣus.
There is a deity named Mārīcī who constantly travels before the sun and moon.
That Mārīcī deity—
No one can see it, no one can seize it; it cannot be deceived by others, nor bound by others;
no one can claim its wealth as a debt.
"Enemies will not be able to find an opportunity against them.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"If there is anyone who knows the name of that goddess Mārīcī..."
That person cannot be seen nor can they be seized;
they cannot be deceived by others, nor can their wealth and property be claimed as debt by others,
nor can enemies find any opportunity against them.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"If there are sons or daughters of good family who know the name of that goddess Mārīcī,"
One should speak thus:
"I, the disciple so-and-so,
because I know the name of that goddess Mārīcī."
No one can see me; no one can seize me. No one can deceive me; no one can bind me.
No one can demand my wealth or property from me.
"An enemy shall not be able to find an opportunity against me.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"This Mārīcī-devī possesses a dhāraṇī mantra."
The protector spoke this mantra:
*Tadyathā | Akāmāsi makāmāsi cibharāmāsi cibharāmāsi mahācibharāmāsi antali-dhānamāsi | Protect me on the path.*
Protect me while traveling on the road;
protect me during the day and protect me at night;
protect me among enemies and protect me from the perils of kings.
Protect me amidst the peril of bandits;
protect me amidst the peril of water; protect me amidst the peril of fire;
protect me amidst the plague of pestilence—*akule akule anuricche*.
Kili kili, ānti ānti. At all places and at all times,
protect my disciple [Name], svāhā.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family—
whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās— "
If kings, ministers, and all the people hear this *Mārīcī-dhāraṇī* mantra and receive and uphold it with single-minded devotion, [they shall attain protection].
They shall not be harmed by any of the aforementioned evils.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"If there are sons or daughters of good family..."
Those who copy, receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra should single-mindedly observe the fast and purify a room,
smearing the floor with fragrant mud.
If one recites and maintains this *Mārīcī-devī-dhāraṇī* mantra for seven days and seven nights,
completing one hundred and eight repetitions,
then all enemies and bandits encountered in every battle array [shall be overcome].
All shall lay down their weapons.
While traveling, one should write out this dhāraṇī;
whether it is placed within one's topknot or within one's clothing, one should carry it with oneself at all times.
No evil whatsoever shall be able to inflict harm;
all shall retreat and disperse, with none daring to confront it.
Should one encounter illness, [it shall likewise be overcome].
One should invite a bhikṣu of pure precepts, as well as a bhikṣuṇī, an upāsaka,
and an upāsikā. As before, one should purify a room, smear the floor with fragrant mud,
burn various kinds of famous incense, and set out seven trays of fruits and cakes.
Spread five-colored cloths and arrange five-colored rice offerings.
Invoke the deity Mārīcī and light lamps to maintain a continuous illumination for seven days and seven nights.
If one recites this *Mārīcī-devī Dhāraṇī Sūtra* two hundred times,
all disease-demons will give rise to a heart of compassion.
If released upon the sick person, they will immediately recover.
If one is detained by local officials,
one should likewise prepare offerings and arrange seats in a purified room according to the ritual rules as described before.
They lit lamps to continue the illumination for seven days and seven nights,
reciting this *Mārīcī-devī-dhāraṇī-sūtra* five hundred times.
Having obtained their wishes, they prepared a vegetarian feast and concluded the assembly.
All calamities and hardships will be extinguished and eliminated without exception.
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, all the bhikṣus were filled with great joy; they believed, accepted, and upheld it.
The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Goddess Mārīcī Spoken by the Buddha.
